title: Characteristic squares and diffractive commutants
reviewed_arguments: S1 proves all positive powers by explicit derivative bounds and last-zero/FTC gluing. The compact-average estimate proves its concavity inequality and includes every parameter derivative.

The exponential cutoff and its derivative satisfy every power estimate, with explicit polynomial domination. S2 takes the smooth square root before applying the exact U014 even descent and full-neighborhood extension.
S3 proves half-space access to the zero set in all tangential, interior and inward cases. It gives every derivative of the flat errors an arbitrarily high power of the defining function.
S4 dominates even a discontinuous locally bounded flat error by multiplicative smoothing of its monotone envelope. The differentiated kernels and all flatness estimates are explicit.

S5 removes the full linear remainder at both real roots, proves its flatness, and dominates it for negative r. The resulting quadratic inequality holds for every real normal covariable; it is equality for nonnegative r.
S6 proves all homogeneous orders and the squared localization for either sign of p. M0 proves the real, complex and finite-rank nonpositive symbol matrices without an operator positivity claim.
S7 makes the normal coefficient a negative smooth square and proves smooth division, including every derivative of the adjusted quotient on the negative-r side.
S8 retains arbitrary tangential dependence of the principal symbol and the exact Hamilton sign. All cutoff derivatives are kept in the incoming region separated from glancing.
The two commutants have the stated homogeneous degrees and nonzero boundary square. Exact DS32–DS33 prove row independence for two small widths, with quantitative denominator and determinant bounds.
All three exercises have complete solutions. The three-panel illustration reproduces DS36 and DS37 exactly and identifies its geometric limitations.
Five finite groups with 177 cases supplement the proofs. All 328 formulae and 37 labelled displays render; all 15 final captures were actually inspected.

The normal commutant is not claimed admissible in the Dirichlet weak form. The H1 boundary functional and natural-dual source still need full analytic treatment; strict propagation and the whole course remain unfinished.
